gaps.sentence: It gets bitterly ___ here in January.
gaps.explanation: bitterly cold is the fixed collocation for extremely cold weather.

gaps.sentence: I'm ___ a course in web design this term.
gaps.explanation: do a course is the British English collocation for studying on a course.

gaps.sentence: The committee will ___ a decision next week.
gaps.explanation: make a decision is the fixed collocation; we do not 'do' or 'give' a decision.

gaps.sentence: The children ___ great fun at the party.
gaps.explanation: have fun / have great fun is the fixed collocation; 'made fun' means mocked someone.

gaps.sentence: The storm ___ a lot of damage to the roof.
gaps.explanation: do damage to something is the collocation; past tense 'did' is needed here.

gaps.sentence: The ___ traffic added an hour to our journey.
gaps.explanation: heavy traffic means a lot of vehicles on the road; 'thick traffic' is not standard.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a serious accident on his motorbike last year.
gaps.explanation: have an accident is the fixed collocation for being involved in one.

gaps.sentence: The roads were almost empty — the traffic was surprisingly ___.
gaps.explanation: light traffic means few vehicles on the road; its opposite is heavy traffic.
